sections.title: Who receives the action?
sections.content:
In Spanish, the presence or absence of a reflexive pronoun clearly tells the listener whether an action is performed on oneself or on something/someone else:
- **Lavar**: *Lavo los platos* (I wash dishes) vs. **Lavarse**: *Me lavo las manos* (I wash my hands).
- **Despertar**: *Despierto a mi hijo* (I wake my son up) vs. **Despertarse**: *Me despierto* (I wake up).
- **Poner**: *Pongo el libro en la mesa* (I put the book on the table) vs. **Ponerse**: *Me pongo el sombrero* (I put on the hat).

items.spanish: Carlos lava su bicicleta los sábados.
items.english: Carlos washes his bicycle on Saturdays.

items.spanish: Carlos se lava las manos antes de comer.
items.english: Carlos washes his hands before eating.

items.spanish: La alarma me despierta a las seis.
items.english: The alarm wakes me up at six.

items.spanish: Yo me despierto antes de la alarma.
items.english: I wake up before the alarm.

sections.content: When an action affects someone else, never use the reflexive pronoun *se/me/te* for the subject; use standard direct objects or the personal *a* (*Despierto a Meg*).
